content.title: Detroit Tigers beat Cardinals 4-0 in home opener at Comerica Park
content.text: Updated April 3, 2026, 3:50 p.m. ETThe Detroit Tigers gave their fans a shutout victory to celebrate at their 2026 home opener.The Tigers (3-4) beat the St. Louis Cardinals (4-3) 4-0 on Friday, March 3, at the home opener at Comerica Park in Detroit to snap a four-game losing streak. Lefty starter Framber Valdez had another impressive outing, pitching six scoreless innings in his first game in a Tigers uniform at Comerica Park.It was also the first MLB home game for rookie Kevin McGonigle, who went 1-for-4 with a double on an active defensive day for the team's top prospect. McGonigle was part of six defensive outs at third base, further demonstrating his big league readiness on the infield.Watch Tigers baseball on FuboRight fielder Kerry Carpenter and left fielder Riley Greene each had two hits, while catcher Dillon Dingler had the biggest blast of the afternoon with a two-run home run in the fourth inning to open the scoring.Here's how it all went down.Tigers vs Cardinals Opening Day highlights Tigers win 4-0FINAL: Tigers 4, Cardinals 0.Tigers lefty Tyler Holton made quick work of the Cardinals in the ninth inning to lock down the win for Detroit at the home opener. The Tigers are now 3-4 on the season after snapping their four-game losing streak. Tigers home opener attendanceThe Tigers announced a sellout crowd of 45,008 for today's home opener, the largest home opener crowd in nearly a decade. Kyle Finnegan pitches scoreless eighthMiddle 8th: Tigers 4, Cardinals 0.Tigers reliever Kyle Finnegan began the eighth inning by allowing a single to catcher Iván Herrera and walking first baseman Alec Burleson. He then got the first out of the inning by striking out pinch hitter Nolan Gorman.From there, it was rookie Kevin McGonigle, who got the second and third outs of the inning on consecutive ground balls to third base. The Tigers have a 4-0 lead. Will Vest in for Framber ValdezTop 7th: Tigers 4, Cardinals 0.That is indeed the end of Framber Valdez's afternoon. Will Vest comes in to replace him in the seventh inning.Valdez's final line: 6 IP, 3 H, 0 R, 2 BB, 5K. He is in line for the win. Javier Báez hits RBI singleEnd 6th: Tigers 4, Cardinals 0.Tigers shortstop Javier Báez smoked a single through the hole between shortstop and second base, driving in center fielder Parker Meadows from second base and extending the Tigers lead to 4-0.It was Báez's second hit of the day and the Tigers' 10th hit of the afternoon. Framber Valdez pitches clean sixth inningMiddle 6th: Tigers 3, Cardinals 0.Through six innings, Tigers starter Framber Valdez has given up zero runs and three hits while striking out five batters and walking two. That lowers his season ERA to 0.75.Valdez has not been officially replaced yet. However, with the lefty at 91 pitches, the Tigers will likely opt to bring in a reliever to start the seventh inning. Riley Greene RBI gives Tigers 3-0 leadBottom 5th: Tigers 2, Cardinals 0.Tigers rookie Kevin McGonigle hit a one-out double down the left field line for his first hit at Comerica Park. A ground ball to pitcher Michael McGreevy led to McGonigle being thrown out at third, however, to take him off the basepaths.Cardinals lefty reliever Justin Bruihl then came into the game to pitch to right fielder Kerry Carpenter, who singled up the middle to keep the inning alive. Left fielder Riley Greene then hit an RBI single in the exact same place to extend Detroit's lead to 3-0. It is Greene's fifth RBI of the season and 500th hit of his career. Dillon Dingler hits two-run home runBottom 4th: Tigers 2, Cardinals 0.Tigers left fielder Riley Greene smacked a one-out double to right-center field for his first hit of the game, but he would be one-upped soon after.Tigers catcher Dillon Dingler sent a no-doubter fly ball past the back wall in left-center field, marking a two-run home run and his second home run of the season. Dingler has both Tigers home runs in 2026. Framber Valdez escapes bases-loaded jamMiddle 4th: Tigers 0, Cardinals 0.Cardinals first baseman Alex Burleson led off the fourth inning with a single, and consecutive strikeouts to third baseman Ramón Urías and Jordan Walker followed. Tigers starter Framber Valdez looked like he got the third out of the inning on a ground ball to first baseman Spencer Torkelson, but Valdez dropped the throw from Torkelson to allow Yohel Pozo on with an error.Valdez then walked second baseman Thomas Saggese to load the bases, prompting a visit from Tigers pitching coach Chris Fetter. But once again, Valdez escaped trouble with a soft flyout from left fielder José Fermín to end the inning. Javier Báez thrown out trying to scoreEnd 3rd: Tigers 0, Cardinals 0.A one-out single from Tigers shortstop Javier Báez led to a runner in scoring position after Báez stole second. With two outs, designated hitter Gleyber Torres poked a single to shallow right field, and Báez was sent home by third base coach Joey Cora.However, Cardinals right fielder Jordan Walker unleashed a missile to home and nailed Báez at the plate for the third out of the inning. We are still scoreless. Framber Valdez escapes two-out jamMiddle 3rd: Tigers 0, Cardinals 0.Victor Scott II recorded the first Cardinals hit with a two-out single just over third baseman Kevin McGonigle in the top of the third inning. Shortstop Masyn Winn followed that with a single of his own to right-center field, moving Scott to third base, bringing a runner into scoring position for the first time this game.However, Tigers starter Framber Valdez finished off the scoreless inning by inducing a ground ball to shortstop Javier Báez, who tossed it to second baseman Zach McKinstry to get Winn out at second. Brandon Inge throws out first pitchIf you missed it, here's a replay of former Tiger Brandon Inge throwing to his former teammate (and current Tiger) Justin Verlander. Kevin McGonigle makes first play at Comerica ParkMiddle 2nd: Tigers 0, Cardinals 0.Cardinals designated hitter Yohel Pozo hit a two-out grounder to Tigers rookie Kevin McGonigle, who scooped it up and threw out Pozo at first for the final out of the inning.No score through two innings. Kerry Carpenter misses home run by inchesEnd 1st: Tigers 0, Cardinals 0.Tigers rookie Kevin McGonigle sent a ball 403 feet to center field on the second pitch of his first at-bat at Comerica Park. That would have been a home run in many parts of the stadium, but the ball fell harmlessly into Victor Scott's glove right at the warning track.Right fielder Kerry Carpenter smacked a two-out single 110 mph off the bat that just missed a home run by inches off the right-field wall. Left fielder Riley Greene couldn't drive him in, however, as his flyout to left-center finished off the inning. Framber Valdez pitches 1-2-3 first inningMiddle 1st: Tigers 0, Cardinals 0.Cardinals shortstop Masyn Winn lined out to left field to start the game, and Tigers starter Framber Valdez followed that by striking out catcher Iván Herrera in the next plate appearance. Valdez covered first base on a ground ball to first baseman Spencer Torkelson to end the inning – a solid 1-2-3 opening frame for "La Grasa." Framber Valdez introducedMaking his Comerica Park debut (at least in a Tigers uniform) is lefty Framber Valdez, who is starting the home opener. He got a big ovation as he ran onto the field. Justin Verlander introducedThe Tigers were introduced on the field, with fans giving loud ovations for rookie Kevin McGonigle and ace Tarik Skubal.But the loudest ovation was for starter Justin Verlander, who is returning to Comerica Park as a Tiger for the first time since 2017. New food at Comerica ParkPierogi nachos? Turkey leg? A grilled cheese Sonoran dog?These are just some of the new food items at Comerica Park this year for fans to enjoy, and our Susan Selasky has the full breakdown here. Home opener game-time temperatureThe Tigers announced the game-time temperature is 73℉ about 30 minutes before first pitch. Even with the sun behind the clouds, it still feels warm with very few fans wearing sweaters or jackets right now. Tigers walkup songsTigers batters and pitchers have revealed their walkup songs for the 2026 season. Some of them will be familiar (Tarik Skubal will still run out to Jay-Z's "Holy Grail," for example) while others are brand new. Party at Comerica ParkEven if you don't have a ticket for the game, a good time can still be had just outside Comerica Park, with tailgates and parties all around the stadium and even more events downtown. Cardinals lineupThe St. Louis Cardinals are running out a lineup of young, mostly homegrown players for today's game.SS Masyn Winn.C Iván Herrera.1B Alec Burleson.3B Ramón Urías.RF Jordan Walker.DH Yohel Pozo.2B Thomas Saggese.LF José Fermín.CF Victor Scott II.SP - Michael McGreevy. Justin Verlander catching ceremonial first pitchTigers righty Justin Verlander isn't pitching today, but he will be a part of the pregame ceremonies.During his press availability, Verlander said that former Tigers utility player Brandon Inge, who is throwing the ceremonial first pitch for today's home opener, texted Verlander saying he had better catch his pitch. Verlander confirmed he would do so. Colt Keith not in starting lineupTigers infielder Colt Keith has been one of the Tigers' best hitters so far this season, slashing .364/.417/.545 over 24 plate appearances. But despite his hot start, Keith doesn't appear in the lineup, with Spencer Torkelson playing first base, Zach McKinstry playing second and Kevin McGonigle playing third. Tigers lineupThe Tigers have released their starting lineup for today's game, with rookie Kevin McGonigle leading off and Colt Keith, one of the team's hottest hitters early in the season, not starting.3B Kevin McGonigle.DH Gleyber Torres.RF Kerry Carpenter.LF Riley Greene.C Dillon Dingler.2B Zach McKinstry.1B Spencer Torkelson.CF Parker Meadows.SS Javier Báez.SP Framber Valdez. Good morning!The Tigers social media team posted some sunrise pictures this morning, and you need to give them a look.What time is Tigers vs Cardinals Opening Day?Time: 1:10 p.m. ET.Date: Friday, April 2.Location: Comerica Park, Detroit.What channel is Tigers vs Cardinals Opening Day?Channel: Detroit SportsNet, Fox-2 Detroit (WJBK).First pitch: 1:10 p.m. ET.Streaming: Fubo, MLB.tv.Radio: WXYT-FM (97.1).Friday's home opener can be watched on either the new Detroit SportsNet or locally on Fox-2 Detroit (WJBK), while the game can be streamed on Fubo (which carries DSN).Watch Tigers home opener on FuboTigers home opener vs Cardinals pitching matchupDET: LHP Framber Valdez (0-0, 1.50 ERA).STL: RHP Michael McGreevy (0-0, 0.00 ERA).Comerica Park detailsAddress: 2100 Woodward Ave, Detroit, MI, 48201.Gates open: 11:30 a.m. ET.First pitch: 1:10 p.m. ET.Public transit: Montcalm St. (Q-Line), Woodward & Columbia (Line 4).Parking info: Via Tigers website.Note: The People Mover will remain closed through Opening Day weekend as repairs continue.Road closures for Opening Day in DetroitAll streets around Comerica Park will be restricted from vehicle traffic during home games, with road closures in effect approximately 3 hours before each game time, according to the Tigers.The map below shows routes to Comerica Park parking areas during restricted traffic for the Tigers’ home opener (tap here for larger size).Detroit Opening Day weatherFriday is expected to be unseasonably warm across metro Detroit, with highs in the mid-70s – about 20 degrees above normal for early April, said National Weather Service meteorologist Kevin Kacan. Skies will be mostly cloudy after a possible brief morning shower, and winds may gust up to 25 mph.Comerica Park food and drink optionsFans at Comerica Park for the Tigers’ 2026 home opener can expect new twists on ballpark favorites, local eats and value options. Highlights include the Tiger Tail footlong corn dog, pierogi nachos, a smoked short rib sandwich and offerings from Detroit-area restaurants like Breadless, Slows Bar-BQ, Fairway Packing Co., Bert’s Marketplace and Taqueria El Rey.Value deals return, including $9.42 hot dog meals, $12.50 pizza meals, $5 beers and more.Who is throwing the first pitch for the Tigers home opener?Longtime Tigers utility man Brandon Inge will throw the first pitch for Detroit's home opener on Friday. Inge played for the Tigers for 12 seasons between 2001-12 and accumulated 18.6 Baseball Reference WAR during his time in Detroit.Free Press reporters Nour Rahal and Susan Selasky contributed to this article.Need to catch up on the news during your lunch break?
